why: Past AQI only (lags 0-6, rolling windows ending at D). AQI(D) is complete at 24:00 of D. Gaps filled causally (same-day neighbours, ffill, train-period climatology).
Pollutant daily means/8-h maxima and intraday shape of day D. These are inputs to AQI, but of day D, not D+1, so they are legitimate lags.
Valid-hour counts and missing flags of day D; sensor gaps are informative (more gaps on polluted days).
Mean AQI/PM2.5 of OTHER stations in the same city/state on day D. Same-time readings of OTHER stations at D+1 are NOT used.
OBSERVED weather from the station's own CPCB sensors (WS, RH, AT, SR, BP, RF, WD) for day D. Reported live, so available at issue time.

feature group / column: Weather of the target day D+1 (observed)
why: Observed future weather = leakage for a true forecast. We use observed weather up to D only (no weather forecast input).
Published ~5 days after real time (ERA5T), so even day-D values would not exist at 24:00 of D.
NASA FIRMS MODIS detections up to day D (near real-time product exists).
Day of year/week, Diwali distance, lockdown flag of D+1: known in advance.
Coordinates, elevation, region; station-month AQI climatology computed from the TRAINING period only.

feature group / column: AQI(D+1), AQI_cat, AQI_driver, sub-indices SI_* of D+1
why: Deterministic function of the target day's pollutant concentrations: hands the model the answer.

feature group / column: Pollutant concentrations of D+1 (PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3)
why: Inputs of the target AQI: not available when the forecast is issued.
Kept in the table for diagnostics only, never a feature.
Would mix D+1.. values into day-D features. All windows are trailing; linear interpolation was evaluated only in the offline reconstruction test.
Stuck-sensor and spike checks use only data of the same day, so cleaning of day D never looks at D+1.
Medians, climatology, StandardScaler and PCA are fitted on training rows only, then applied to val/test.
